about: Contract for sanitizeFilename() in src/shared/filenames.ts and its Python port in the native host: both must map every input below to its expected output.

Rules, in order: (1) unpaired UTF-16 surrogates become U+FFFD; (2) < > : " / \ | ? *, control characters (Cc: U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F), format characters (Cf) and noncharacters (U+FDD0-FDEF, U+xFFFE, U+xFFFF) become one space each; (3) every run of whitespace (U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) becomes one space; (4) spaces, dots and tildes are stripped from both ends; (5) the name is cut to maxLength UTF-16 code units, one fewer if the cut would split a surrogate pair, then spaces, dots and tildes are stripped from the end again; (6) a reserved name gets a '_' prefix and step 5 runs again; (7) an empty result becomes '_'.

Reserved: the part before the first dot, with trailing spaces removed, is CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, CLOCK$, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9 or COM/LPT followed by superscript 1, 2 or 3 (U+00B9, U+00B2, U+00B3), compared ASCII-case-insensitively; or the whole name is desktop.ini or thumbs.db.
Lengths count UTF-16 code units (an emoji counts 2), not code points as Python's len() does.
'%' is kept; the host doubles it for yt-dlp after sanitising.
buildStem cases are for the JavaScript side; every expected stem is also a fixed point of sanitizeFilename.
This file is pure ASCII: every other character is written as a \u escape.
